props.gloss_en: the mishna: one may not light with burning-oil on a Festival
what is the reason [one may not light with burning-oil on a Festival]? because one does not burn consecrated things on a Festival
one does not burn consecrated things on a Festival
Chizkiya: the source is 'you shall leave none of it until morning, and what is left of it until morning [you shall burn]' (Ex 12:10)
Chizkiya: the verse need not say 'until morning' [a second time]; why does it say it? the verse comes to give it a second morning for its burning
Abaye: the source is 'the olah of Shabbat on its Shabbat' (Num 28:10)
Abaye: and not a weekday olah on Shabbat, and not a weekday olah on a Festival
Rava: the source is 'that alone may be done for you' (Ex 12:16)
Rava: 'that' -- and not its enablers
Rava: 'alone' -- and not circumcision out of its time, which [otherwise] would come by a kal vachomer
Rav Ashi: the source is 'shabbaton'
Rav Ashi: 'shabbaton' is a positive command; so a Festival is [governed by] a positive command and a prohibition
Rav Ashi: and a positive command does not override a prohibition together with a positive command
it is on a Festival that [lighting with burning-oil] is forbidden; on a weekday it is fine
Rav: just as there is a mitzva to burn consecrated things that became impure, so there is a mitzva to burn teruma that became impure
Rav: and the Torah said: at the time of its destruction, benefit from it

Rabba bar Avuh: 'I have given you the charge of My terumot' (Num 18:8) -- the verse speaks of two terumot, one pure and one impure; and the Merciful One said 'to you' -- it shall be yours, to kindle it under your dish
R' Yochanan: 'nor have I destroyed of it while impure' (Deut 26:14) -- of IT you may not burn, but you may burn oil of teruma that became impure
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'you shall give him' (Deut 18:4) -- him, and not his fire; by implication, [impure teruma] is fit for his fire
the surviving reading: ממנו excludes TERUMA from the burning-while-impure prohibition
the rival reading: ממנו excludes KODESH -- impure consecrated oil may be burned
kodesh carries piggul, notar, [a] korban, me'ila and karet, and is forbidden to the acute mourner (the mnemonic bundle kept composite, as in Yevamot 73b)
teruma carries death, the added fifth, no redemption, and is forbidden to non-priests
alternatively: kodesh is the stringent one, for it is punished with karet
